title: WebAuthn request that needs a security-key PIN crashes the browser process on Linux
body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.4.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS (Arch-based), Linux 7.1.8-1-cachyos, KDE Plasma 6 (Wayland) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version None found. 43.4.1, 42.9.0, and 39.8.10 also crashed with SIGTRAP, but those runs followed an earlier crash that had left the YubiKey 5 unresponsive, so they are consistent with the finding rather than clean data. The clean single-key runs below are on 43.4.0. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When a WebAuthn request reaches a USB security key that requires a PIN and Electron has no PIN prompt to show, the request should reject (for example with `NotAllowedError`) and the app should keep running. ### Actual Behavior The browser process dies with SIGTRAP from a CHECK about 0.7 s after launch, during `navigator.credentials.create()` and before the key is touched. With `--enable-logging=stderr --vmodule=device_event_log_impl=1`, the FIDO log ends right after Chromium reads the key's PIN retry count: ``` FIDO: DEBUG: fido_device.cc:70 The device supports the CTAP2 protocol. FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:91 <- 0x6 (kAuthenticatorClientPin) {1: 2, 2: 7} FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:188 -> {5: 0} FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:91 <- 0x6 (kAuthenticatorClientPin) {1: 2, 2: 1} FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:188 -> {3: 8} ``` `{5: 0}` answers the UV-retries query and `{3: 8}` reports 8 PIN retries. Results with the gist on 43.4.0: | Keys plugged in | Result | |---|---| | YubiKey 5 only | Crash during `create()`, no touch | | YubiKey 4 only | `create()` OK, `get()` OK | | Both; YubiKey 4 touched | `create()` OK, `get()` OK; the log shows a clean cancel of the YubiKey 5's operation | The YubiKey 5 (USB `1050:0406`, firmware 5.8.0) reports `alwaysUv: true`, `uv: true`, `clientPin: true`, `bioEnroll: true`, `makeCredUvNotRqd: false`, and `pinUvAuthToken: true`, so every operation needs user verification. The YubiKey 4 (USB `1050:0407`) is U2F only. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/nisavid/a7e5438b6ceef5a0761898dc99ec6b64 ### Additional Information The gist is a minimal main-process app that serves `index.html` on `http://localhost` and runs `navigator.credentials.create()` for a non-resident credential with `userVerification: "discouraged"`, then `navigator.credentials.get()` with that credential. `get()` takes `userVerification` from the `uv` query parameter (default `discouraged`); `REPRO_QUERY='?uv=preferred'` sets it, which the crashing runs used, though the single-key run crashed inside `create()` before `get()` ran. Run it with a PIN-protected FIDO2 key plugged in: ``` electron . --enable-logging=stderr --vmodule=device_event_log_impl=1 ``` This is narrower than #24573, which tracks the missing Linux FIDO2 PIN UI: here a request that needs the PIN takes the browser process down instead of rejecting. It surfaced in the Proton Pass desktop app (`/usr/lib/electron43/electron /usr/share/proton-pass/app.asar`), whose in-app sign-in crashed three times on 2026-09-24 with a main-thread stack identical to the gist's. Chrome was not tested.
In-depth investigation

The distro `electron43` binary is stripped. `systemd-coredump` labels frame 0 `cppgc::internal::FatalImpl`, but that 7-byte exported symbol (`push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; int3; ud2`) is an identical-code-folded `IMMEDIATE_CRASH` stub, so the name is a misattribution. Identifying the other frames by the source-path strings their functions reference gives: a `device.mojom.HidConnection` read, then `device/fido/hid/fido_hid_device.cc` (message received), then the `device/fido/ctap2_device_operation.h` response callback, then the crash stub. The gist's core has the same stack hash as the Proton Pass cores. My reading, as inference: the key's `alwaysUv` makes the request need PIN/UV, the request handler moves on to PIN collection after reading the retry counts, and with no PIN UI on Linux the browser process hits a CHECK instead of failing the request.
